title: Does volunteering help with college applications? · AquaTerra
description: Volunteering can give you dated, documented work to describe in a college application. What AquaTerra members can show, and what no one can promise.
lede: Volunteering can give you real, dated work to describe on a college application, but no organisation can promise how a college will weigh it. At AquaTerra, every drive is written up on the site with its date, its place and what the team did, so members have a public record to point to.

sections.heading: what a public record looks like
body: Every AquaTerra drive has a write-up on the site, and each one carries the date, the place, how many people came, the objective and a key figure. AquaTerra has written up {drives} drives since {firstYear}, so a drive you took part in can be found by its title and date.

A few examples show the range. The Sunderbans 8.0 trip in December 2025 had a team of fifteen and notes more than 120 checkups. The Canal Side Park planting in June 2025 notes 110 saplings planted, and the Bangur dog drive of September 2025 notes 55 dogs fed.

sections.heading: what members actually do
body: Across {placesCount} places, {volunteers} volunteer turnouts have gone out. The work is hands-on and varied: feeding dogs, planting saplings, running art and reading sessions for children, handing out food and sharbat, and medical checkups on the Sundarbans trips.
Students aged 14 to 19 take part in the same drives, and each write-up says what the team did on the day. The write-up is the part a reader can see, so it helps to keep your own notes as you go.

sections.heading: what no one can promise
body: AquaTerra cannot promise that a drive will change an application. Members can ask for a certificate of the drives they attended, but no one can promise an admissions result. Ask the college what it values in volunteering before you decide what to put forward.
The public write-ups give you something to point to. How a college reads them is up to the college, and a drive should be described for what it was: the work, the place and your own part in it.

sections.heading: how to build a record that holds up
body: Join a team by signing in with Google and waiting for approval. Members are students aged 14 to 19. Take part in the drives that interest you most, and stay with one series, such as the dog feeding drives or the children's workshops, so your record shows repeated work rather than one day out.

Keep a dated list of the drives you joined, with the title, the date, the place and what you did, and put the matching write-up from the site next to each entry. That is the record a reader can check without relying on you.

sections.heading: where to start
body: Start with the [volunteering for teens](/impact/volunteering-for-teens-in-kolkata) page, then read about [student leadership](/impact/student-leadership) if you want to lead a team. The [your first year](/impact/your-first-year) page sets out the first months with the team.
For questions about joining, the [FAQ](/faq) answers the common ones, and the [contact page](/contact) reaches the team directly.

learnings: Choose dated, public work over a bare claim. Each AquaTerra drive has a write-up with its date and place, which is something you can point to.
Stay with one series for a while. Repeated visits to the same kind of work, such as the Tails and Treats dog drives or the Grow Green planting days, make a clearer record than one day out.
Ask the college what it values before you decide. Its own rules decide how it reads volunteering.
Keep your own dated list. The title, date, place and what you did for each drive is what you will need to describe it later.

faqs.q: Does volunteering help with college applications?
faqs.a: Volunteering can give you real, dated work to describe in an application. AquaTerra cannot promise that any college will count it, but every drive is written up on its site with the date, the place and what the team did.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra give a certificate for volunteering?
faqs.a: Yes, on request: every drive a member turns up to is logged against their name by whoever runs it, and members can ask HR for a certificate that says so (see the [join page](/join)). What no one can promise is how a college will weigh it. What AquaTerra also publishes is the write-up for each drive on its site.

faqs.q: What can a 16-year-old do at AquaTerra?
faqs.a: Members aged 14 to 19 take part in drives such as feeding stray dogs, planting saplings, running children's workshops, handing out food and sharbat, and medical checkups on Sundarbans trips. Sign in with Google and wait for approval to join.

faqs.q: How do I show volunteer work on a college application?
faqs.a: Keep a dated list of each drive you joined, with its title, date, place and what you did, and match it to the AquaTerra write-up for that drive. Describe your own role in your own words.

faqs.q: Is volunteering with a student NGO useful for teenagers in Kolkata?
faqs.a: What a student gets from it depends on the drives they choose. AquaTerra gives members aged 14 to 19 a public, dated record of repeated work in Kolkata.
